feed.title: Pronounce — recent dictionary additions
feed.subtitle: How engineers actually pronounce project / product / jargon names. Community-maintained.

entry.title: .NET — dot net
entry.summary: .NET is pronounced "dot net" (/ˈdɑːt nɛt/). The leading dot is spoken: 'dot net', /dɑːt nɛt/. Nobody says 'period net' or drops the prefix.

entry.title: ASP.NET — A S P dot net
entry.summary: ASP.NET is pronounced "A S P dot net" (/ˌeɪ ɛs ˈpiː dɑːt nɛt/). Letters, then the framework: 'ay-ess-pee dot net'. The dot is part of the name and always spoken.

entry.title: SQL Server — S Q L server
entry.summary: SQL Server is pronounced "S Q L server" (/ˌɛs kjuː ˈɛl ˈsɜːrvər/). Both readings are current for Microsoft's database: letters ('ess-kyoo-ell server') and 'sequel server'. Microsoft itself uses both in its own talks, so neither is wrong — the letters are the safer default in an international room.

entry.title: Objective-C — objective C
entry.summary: Objective-C is pronounced "objective C" (/əbˈdʒɛktɪv ˈsiː/). The C is the letter: 'objective see', /əbˈdʒɛktɪv siː/. Stress sits on the second syllable of 'objective'.

entry.title: WPF — W P F
entry.summary: WPF is pronounced "W P F" (/ˌdʌbəljuː piː ˈɛf/). Windows Presentation Foundation is always three letters in speech: 'double-you-pee-eff'. Never expanded aloud.

entry.title: WCF — W C F
entry.summary: WCF is pronounced "W C F" (/ˌdʌbəljuː siː ˈɛf/). Windows Communication Foundation: three letters, 'double-you-see-eff'.

entry.title: JSP — J S P
entry.summary: JSP is pronounced "J S P" (/ˌdʒeɪ ɛs ˈpiː/). JavaServer Pages is always the letters: 'jay-ess-pee'. Never 'jisp'.

entry.title: VBA — V B A
entry.summary: VBA is pronounced "V B A" (/ˌviː biː ˈeɪ/). Visual Basic for Applications: 'vee-bee-ay'. The letters, not 'vuh-bah'.

entry.title: VB.NET — V B dot net
entry.summary: VB.NET is pronounced "V B dot net" (/ˌviː biː ˈdɑːt nɛt/). 'V-B dot net': two letters, a spoken dot, then 'net'.

entry.title: Xcode — ex code
entry.summary: Xcode is pronounced "ex code" (/ˈɛks koʊd/). The X is the letter: 'eks-code' /ˈɛks koʊd/, not 'ks-code' and not 'cross-code'.

entry.title: Oracle — OR uh kul
entry.summary: Oracle is pronounced "OR uh kul" (/ˈɔːrəkəl/). First-syllable stress, three syllables: OR-uh-kul, /ˈɔːrəkəl/ — not 'oh-RAK-ul'.

entry.title: Eclipse — ih clips
entry.summary: Eclipse is pronounced "ih clips" (/ɪˈklɪps/). The IDE splits the community: 'ih-CLIPS' /ɪˈklɪps/, like the astronomical event, against 'ee-CLIPS' /iːˈklɪps/, which the Foundation's own presenters use. Both are heard at every Java conference.

entry.title: MATLAB — MAT lab
entry.summary: MATLAB is pronounced "MAT lab" (/ˈmætlæb/). From MATrix LABoratory: MAT-lab /ˈmætlæb/, one stress on the first syllable, not 'mat-LAB'.

entry.title: LINQ — link
entry.summary: LINQ is pronounced "link" (/lɪŋk/). Language Integrated Query is said as a word, exactly like 'link' /lɪŋk/ — never spelled out as L-I-N-Q.

entry.title: Apache — uh patch ee
entry.summary: Apache is pronounced "uh patch ee" (/əˈpætʃi/). Named after the Native American tribe: uh-PATCH-ee /əˈpætʃi/, three syllables. Not 'uh-PATCH', not 'AP-uh-chee', and never the French reading.

entry.title: OpenCV — open C V
entry.summary: OpenCV is pronounced "open C V" (/ˌoʊpən ˌsiː ˈviː/). The CV is two letters: 'open see-vee'. Never 'open-cuhv'.

entry.title: Xamarin — ZAM uh rin
entry.summary: Xamarin is pronounced "ZAM uh rin" (/ˈzæmərɪn/). The X is a /z/: ZAM-uh-rin /ˈzæmərɪn/, stress on the first syllable. Not 'eks-uh-rin'.

entry.title: T-SQL — T sequel
entry.summary: T-SQL is pronounced "T sequel" (/ˌtiː ˈsiːkwəl/). Microsoft's dialect: 'tee-sequel' is the common reading, but plenty of DBAs say the letters 'tee-ess-kyoo-ell'. Both are in circulation inside Microsoft's own docs and talks.

entry.title: ggplot2 — G G plot two
entry.summary: ggplot2 is pronounced "G G plot two" (/ˌdʒiː dʒiː ˈplɑːt tuː/). The grammar-of-graphics package: 'gee-gee-plot-two', with 'gg' as two letters. Never 'g-plot-two'.

entry.title: UITableView — you eye table view
entry.summary: UITableView is pronounced "you eye table view" (/ˌjuː aɪ ˈteɪbəl vjuː/). The UIKit class is read as its prefix letters then the word: 'you-eye table view'. Not 'you-it-able-view' and not 'U-I-table-view'.

entry.title: winapi — win A P I
entry.summary: winapi is pronounced "win A P I" (/wɪn ˌeɪ piː ˈaɪ/). 'win ay-pee-eye': the word 'win', then three letters. Never 'why-nappy'.

entry.title: Delphi — DEL fy
entry.summary: Delphi is pronounced "DEL fy" (/ˈdɛlfaɪ/). The Greek oracle, with a long i: DEL-fy /ˈdɛlfaɪ/, two syllables. Not 'del-fee'.

entry.title: Cordova — cor DOH vuh
entry.summary: Cordova is pronounced "cor DOH vuh" (/kɔːrˈdoʊvə/). Stress on the middle syllable: kor-DOH-vuh /kɔːrˈdoʊvə/, named after the Spanish city.

entry.title: Hibernate — HIGH ber nate
entry.summary: Hibernate is pronounced "HIGH ber nate" (/ˈhaɪbərneɪt/). The English verb, first-syllable stress: HIGH-ber-nate /ˈhaɪbərneɪt/. Not 'hih-BER-nut'.

entry.title: .htaccess — aitch tee access
entry.summary: .htaccess is pronounced "aitch tee access" (/ˌeɪtʃ tiː ˈæksɛs/). Read as the hidden filename it is: 'H-T-access' /eɪtʃ tiː æksɛs/. The leading dot is never spoken, and the T is always there — 'aitch-access' drops a letter.
